title: Beef with Rice and Vegetables (no carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy) with Cheese Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, boiled rice and a mix of vegetables (e.g., bell pepper, zucchini, peas) prepared without carrots, broccoli or dark‑green leafy greens, served with a smooth cheese sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a rich source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.
Rice is a staple carbohydrate worldwide; this recipe uses long‑grain rice that stays separate after cooking.
Cheese sauce is typically made from cream cheese and milk, flavored with herbs and spices.
Excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens makes the dish easier on sensitive stomachs.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Steady energy source
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbohydrates that release glucose slowly, supporting stable energy levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both beef and rice contain B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from sauce
items.content: The cheese sauce adds calcium, contributing to bone health.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Omitting certain high‑fiber vegetables makes the meal gentler on the digestive system.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Cheese sauce can be high in saturated fats; people with high cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauce often contains salt; choose a low‑sodium version if you have hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The sauce may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, combining beef, rice and vegetables on a plate and drizzling with cheese sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months if divided into portions.
